source: Through an assessment of doubling times in transfected and parental cell lines, we confirmed that the expression of CBE, T7 RNAP, AsCas12a ultra, and the CBE sgRNA had minimal or no impact on parasite growth across all three species (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the experiments shown in Figure 3D.

claim: PF16 is a gene encoding a central pair protein of the axoneme that has been demonstrated to be essential for Leishmania flagellar motility.
source: Having established this optimized system, we next decided to target PF16, a gene encoding a central pair protein of the axoneme that has been demonstrated to be essential for Leishmania flagellar motility (Beneke et al., 2017; Engstler and Beneke, 2023; Martel et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: CBE sgRNA PF16-3 induces paralysis in Leishmania parasites by introducing a thymidine homo-polymer ('TTTTT') within the PF16 coding sequence (CDS).
source: For our test, we chose to utilize a previously employed PF16-targeting CBE sgRNA, namely PF16-3. This specific CBE sgRNA induces paralysis in Leishmania parasites by introducing a thymidine homo-polymer ('TTTTT') within the PF16 coding sequence (CDS).
evidence: This is stated as a description of the CBE sgRNA PF16-3.

claim: Just 14 days post transfection, the homo-polymer had been fully introduced in non-clonal L. major populations when using the T7 RNAP promoter-based dual vector system.
source: As anticipated, we observed a significant increase in editing activity in L. major parasites. Just 14 days post transfection, we found that the homo-polymer had been fully introduced in non-clonal populations when using our T7 RNAP promoter-based dual vector system, while no editing could be observed using the ribosomal promoter single-vector system at this time point (Figure 4B, L. major panel).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the experiments shown in Figure 4B.

claim: No editing could be observed using the ribosomal promoter single-vector system at 14 days post transfection in L. major.
source: As anticipated, we observed a significant increase in editing activity in L. major parasites. Just 14 days post transfection, we found that the homo-polymer had been fully introduced in non-clonal populations when using our T7 RNAP promoter-based dual vector system, while no editing could be observed using the ribosomal promoter single-vector system at this time point (Figure 4B, L. major panel).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the experiments shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Just 6 days post transfection, the PF16 target site was fully edited, and the overwhelming majority of all cells were paralyzed in all tested scenarios.
source: Our results clearly showed that just 6 days post transfection, the PF16 target site was fully edited, and the overwhelming majority of all cells were paralyzed in all tested scenarios (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the experiments shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: Editing slowly reversed in L. mexicana cells harboring the pTB107 construct only.
source: However, surprisingly editing slowly reversed in L. mexicana cells harboring the pTB107 construct only (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the experiments shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: The PF16 mutation in L. mexicana is known to be associated with a mild growth defect.
source: Since the PF16 mutation in L. mexicana is known to be associated with a mild growth defect (Beneke et al., 2019), PF16-deficient mutants would eventually be outcompeted over time, leading slowly to the reversal of editing rates.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Both tested L. donovani cell lines and the tested L. mexicana cell line that possessed the pTB107 construct and the tdTomato expression cassette remained paralyzed over the entire observation time.
source: But more importantly the reversal of the PF16 mutation was not observed in any other tested cell line when comparing editing and motility rates 6 and 16 days post transfection. Both tested L. donovani cell lines and the tested L. mexicana cell line that possessed the pTB107 construct and the tdTomato expression cassette (Figure 4A and B) remained paralyzed over the entire observation time.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the experiments shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: Illumina sequencing data showed that there was not a single read of an unedited PF16 CDS in non-clonal paralyzed L. mexicana PF16 mutant populations 16 days post transfection.
source: Analyzing their sequencing data, we did not find a single read of an unedited PF16 CDS (with approximately 35× genome coverage), confirming that indeed all cells within this transfected non-clonal population were completely mutated (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the Illumina sequencing analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: ONT reads could only be mapped to the scenario where cassettes were assumed to be integrated on separate alleles and present in only one copy in the genome.
source: Interestingly, we could only map unique ONT reads to the first scenario, where cassettes were assumed to be integrated on separate alleles and present in only one copy in the genome. These ONT reads covered the entire tdTomato or CBE sgRNA expression cassette, as well as sequences adjacent to homology flanks used for integration (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the ONT sequencing analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: No ONT reads containing the tdTomato or CBE sgRNA cassettes could be linked to any other locus.
source: Importantly, no ONT reads containing the tdTomato or CBE sgRNA cassettes could be linked to any other locus.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the ONT sequencing analysis.

claim: No contigs contained multiple or both, the tdTomato and CBE sgRNA expression cassettes.
source: Moreover, no contigs contained multiple or both, the tdTomato and CBE sgRNA expression cassettes, suggesting again that these cassettes had integrated into opposite alleles and are present in only one copy in the genome.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the ONT sequencing analysis.

claim: Read coverage for the CBE sgRNA cassette, the CDS of tdTomato, and the CDS of the neomycin-resistance marker were approximately half of the read coverage of their harboring chromosome 27.
source: While we found equal read coverage of PF16-mapped reads and the chromosome harboring PF16, read coverage for the CBE sgRNA cassette, the CDS of tdTomato, and the CDS of the neomycin-resistance marker were approximately half of the read coverage of their harboring chromosome 27 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the Illumina sequencing analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Only one CBE sgRNA cassette copy was present per L. mexicana cell.
source: This further confirmed our hypothesis that indeed the CBE sgRNA expression cassette had only been integrated on one allele, and most likely, this meant that only one CBE sgRNA cassette copy was present per L. mexicana cell.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the Illumina sequencing data.

claim: In the previously used single-vector episomal system, approximately one-third of all L. mexicana transfectants possessed more than one CBE-sgRNA expression plasmid.
source: Nevertheless this represents an improvement since, in our previously used single-vector episomal system, approximately one-third of all L. mexicana transfectants possessed more than one CBE-sgRNA expression plasmid, potentially causing combinatorial knockout effects (Engstler and Beneke, 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: All tested L. mexicana clones showed only unique sequencing reads, confirming the integration of only one guide per transfectant.
source: As expected, we found only unique sequencing reads for all tested L. mexicana clones, confirming the integration of only one guide per transfectant (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the Sanger sequencing analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: For L. donovani and L. major, 2 out of 10 sequencing reads showed mixed guide sequences.
source: However, for L. donovani and L. major, 2 out of 10 sequencing reads showed mixed guide sequences (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), suggesting that multiple CBE sgRNAs can be integrated per cell.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the Sanger sequencing analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: The integration of multiple sgRNAs per cell remained random in L. donovani and L. major.
source: Furthermore, the integration of multiple sgRNAs per cell remained random.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the Sanger sequencing analysis.

claim: 24 CBE sgRNAs were designed to introduce a STOP codon within the first half of open-reading frames (ORFs) essential for survival or normal proliferation in promastigote culture.
source: Of these sgRNAs, 24 were designed to introduce a STOP codon within the first half of open-reading frames (ORFs) essential for survival or normal proliferation in promastigote culture.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the sgRNA library design.

source: Notably, only two IFT88, two CRK3, and one CRK2 sgRNAs showed no reduction in abundance, while all other sgRNAs moved significantly outside the 99% confidence interval of the non-targeting controls (Figure 5D).

claim: No substantial differences were observed between the two Rad51 variants used in the CBE system.
source: However, no substantial differences were observed between the two Rad51 variants used in the CBE system (Figure 5D).

claim: The comparison between method v1 and v2 revealed significant improvements: for one sgRNA targeting IFT88 and another targeting CRK3, the new method achieved ~10–20× stronger ratios with substantially reduced error margins for the non-targeting controls.
source: The comparison between method v1 and v2 revealed significant improvements: for one sgRNA targeting IFT88 and another targeting CRK3, the new method achieved ~10–20× stronger ratios with substantially reduced error margins for the non-targeting controls, enabling more accurate classification of fitness-associated genes (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the comparison shown in Figure 5E.

claim: A C-score was implemented that determines the ratio of available cytosines to resulting STOP codons.
source: To address this, we have therefore improved the scoring of previously designed CBE sgRNAs by implementing a C-score that determines the ratio of available cytosines to resulting STOP codons (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated as a description of the improved sgRNA scoring system shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: The new scoring system rates CBE sgRNAs higher when the STOP codon is introduced within positions 4–8 and lower when introduced within positions 11–12.
source: We also considered the position at which the STOP codon would occur and designed a scoring matrix that rates CBE sgRNAs higher when the STOP codon is introduced within positions 4–8 and lower when introduced within positions 11–12 (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated as a description of the improved sgRNA scoring system shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: The introduction of a thymidine homo-polymer ('TTTTT') within the PF16 CDS produces the same motility phenotype observed when using gene replacement strategies for knockout generation.
source: As shown above, the introduction of a thymidine homo-polymer ('TTTTT') within the PF16 CDS produces the same motility phenotype observed when using gene replacement strategies for knockout generation (Beneke et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The ORF was successfully replaced by drug-resistance markers on both alleles.

evidence: This is stated as a result of the experiments shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: Sanger sequencing over integration flanks confirmed the accurate integration of both donor DNA constructs.
source: In addition, we performed Sanger sequencing over integration flanks to verify the integration of donor DNA fragments. This analysis confirmed the accurate integration of both donor DNA constructs (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the Sanger sequencing analysis shown in Figure 6C and D.

claim: Motility analysis on these mutants revealed the expected PF16 motility phenotype.

evidence: This is stated as a result of the motility analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The Leishmania research community faces significant challenges in systematically assessing the function of all genes within the species.
source: The Leishmania research community faces significant challenges in systematically assessing the function of all genes within the species.
evidence: This is stated as a general challenge in the conclusion.

claim: The absence of a functional NHEJ pathway complicates the process of obtaining null mutants in Leishmania.
source: The absence of a functional NHEJ pathway complicates the process of obtaining null mutants, typically demanding the additional use of donor DNA, selection of edits associated with drug resistance, or the time-consuming isolation of clones.
evidence: This is stated as a challenge in the conclusion.

claim: Pooled CRISPR screens that rely solely on sgRNA expression are feasible to some extent for drug-resistance studies in Leishmania.
source: While pooled CRISPR screens that rely solely on sgRNA expression are feasible to some extend for drug-resistance studies in Leishmania (Queffeulou et al., 2024), they are less likely to succeed in fitness-related phenotypic screens.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Pooled CRISPR screens that rely solely on sgRNA expression are less likely to succeed in fitness-related phenotypic screens in Leishmania.
source: While pooled CRISPR screens that rely solely on sgRNA expression are feasible to some extend for drug-resistance studies in Leishmania (Queffeulou et al., 2024), they are less likely to succeed in fitness-related phenotypic screens.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation in the conclusion.
